headline: Oil Surges on Hormuz Tanker Attacks, Heading for Fourth Monthly Gain
summary: Oil prices surged to $117 following new attacks by Iran in the Strait of Hormuz, where five tankers were immobilized, driving prices toward a fourth consecutive monthly gain amid heightened supply risks.
why: Crude oil is a primary global commodity benchmark and key energy input, meaning supply disruptions in critical maritime chokepoints like the Strait of Hormuz immediately impact global energy costs and broader macroeconomic inflation.

impacts.name: Crude oil
impacts.why: Tanker attacks and supply risks in the Strait of Hormuz directly drive up global crude oil prices.
impacts.baseline_rule: first recorded price at or after created_at (15-minute price recorder); end = first price at least 24 h later, within 48 h

why_moved: Geopolitical conflict and tanker attacks in a major oil transit chokepoint restrict supply flows, prompting immediate upward pricing by traders bracing for shortages.
